assertions.detail: the regular representation of H₂(i) = ℂ[σ]/((σ−i)²) in the basis {1, σ−i} is the Jordan block (explicit basis-swap conjugation to !![i,1;0,i]) — the framework's own algebra at the degenerate point carries the unipotent part intrinsically

assertions.name: full_twist_is_PL_transvection
assertions.detail: σ_B(−1)² = 1 + 2N with N = [[1, -1], [1, -1]] rank-1 nilpotent — the full twist (Dehn twist about the two branch points) acts as a Picard–Lefschetz TRANSVECTION on the χ-eigenspace: the unipotent is standard vanishing-cycle geometry, at the same integral point as the Gambaudo–Ghys signature jump (T2)

assertions.name: jordan_module_unique_up_to_iso
assertions.detail: every nonzero 2×2 nilpotent N' = [[p,q],[r,−p]] (p²+qr = 0) is explicitly conjugate to [[0,1],[0,0]] on both parameter branches (q≠0: det P = q; q=0,r≠0: det P = −r) — the 2-dim module with (σ−i)² = 0, σ ≠ i·1 is UNIQUE up to isomorphism: any τ matching the semisimplified data (R1/N3) matches the unipotent part AUTOMATICALLY

assertions.name: skein_consistency_and_two_classes
assertions.detail: on the Jordan module σ⁻¹ = σ − 2i exactly, so σ − σ⁻¹ = (q−q⁻¹)|_{q=i}·1 — the §7a skein relation holds identically; the Hecke relation at q=i admits exactly two module classes (scalar i, Jordan) and T2's monodromy selects Jordan — no further freedom anywhere
